environment.description: Kubernetes 1.28 cluster with namespace-level Pod Security Standards configured via label `pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: baseline` on the migrations namespace. Additionally, a ValidatingAdmissionPolicy (v1beta1, CEL-based) is bound to the namespace with expression `!has(object.spec.volumes) || object.spec.volumes.all(v, !has(v.hostPath))` rejecting any pod spec containing hostPath volumes. The cluster also enforces a Kyverno ClusterPolicy in audit+enforce mode with rule `validate-host-path` matching on kind Pod/Job/CronJob that denies any container with `securityContext.privileged: true` OR any volume of type hostPath. Container image is pulled from a registry with Notary v2 signatures verified by the admission controller. The migration pod runs with `securityContext.runAsNonRoot: true, runAsUser: 65534, readOnlyRootFilesystem: true` with an emptyDir volume for the working directory. Note: the baseline Pod Security Standard does NOT explicitly block all path traversal scenarios - it focuses on preventing host namespace sharing and privileged escalation vectors. The zip slip vulnerability in the code still exists and files can be written outside the intended extraction directory within the container's writable emptyDir mount, but the traversal cannot escape to the host filesystem since no hostPath volume exists and the container has no privileged access to mount or access host paths.

validate.message: hostPath volumes and privileged containers are not allowed

deny.conditions: any hostPath volume OR privileged securityContext
